s01-title: Video five: operations. The parcel state machine, one milestone per scan.
s02-filter: As Quang from operations, we filter waybills by status At Hub. The field is projected: it has its own index, no JSON B scan. Result: one waybill, at the Tan Binh hub.
s03-timeline: Open waybill one. Every scan leaves a trace: six milestones from Created to Delivered, each with a time and a hub. Users cannot write the scan log; only WaybillScanHook appends milestones.
s04-diagram: The state machine is a data table. Each state can move to only a few next states, and Delivered, Cancelled and Returned are final. Before every save, the hook checks this table. A transition not in the table returns a four twenty-two and writes nothing.
s05-skip: A new waybill is at Created. We choose Delivered directly, and the kernel refuses. From Created, only Picked Up or Cancelled are allowed. The scan log still has one milestone.
s06-hub: Picked Up succeeds. At Hub with an empty hub fails, because the hub is required for At Hub. Enter hub Hai Chau and save: it succeeds, and the timeline gains a milestone. The customer care replica also reaches three milestones.
s07-cancel: As Mai, we try to cancel a delivered order. The hook allows it only while the waybill is Created or Picked Up, so it is rejected. After a reload: still Submitted, still Delivered, since both share one transaction.
s08-api: Same rules over REST. Transitions in order return two hundred. Jumping from At Hub to Delivered, or cancelling the order once the waybill is At Hub, returns a four twenty-two, and the order stays Submitted. Desk and API hit the same hook.
s09-code: Developer code: one table, one veto. The NEXT table lists valid transitions; beforeSave throws for any other. On the order side, onCancel allows cancelling only while the waybill is Created or Picked Up, and updates it in the order's transaction.
s10-recap: Recap: projected filters, a hook-only scan log, no skipped states, At Hub needs a hub, and delivered orders cannot be cancelled.
s11-outro: Astra. One platform, every business process. Open source, MIT license.
